subject: Capacity waterfall + deal-trigger matrix for BrightMart commit
messages:
From: Olivia Hart <olivia@brightmart.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightmart.com
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP Q4 + committed capacity question

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs asked us to put together a short RFP for Q4 forecasting — essentially we need a committed capacity proposal that ties to the promotional calendar and a clear view on how Redwood will handle GPU price swings.

Two asks from procurement:
- Illustrative capacity waterfall (baseline -> committed -> burst) by quarter for 12 months.
- A simple matrix showing discounts / crediting if GPU costs move +/- 20% relative to today.

Attached is our procurement outline (BrightMart_RFP_Q4.pdf). Can you send a draft matrix we can review with finance?

Target timeline: internal procurement review by 9/22.

Olivia
Procurement Lead, BrightMart

Attachments: BrightMart_RFP_Q4.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Hart <olivia@brightmart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q4 + committed capacity question

Olivia — thanks, got the RFP. Putting a short matrix together now and looping in Karthik + Marissa for pricing/commit approvals. High level approach below; I'll attach a working waterfall workbook in the next note.

Summary approach (working):
- Baseline (on-demand): expected monthly steady-state tokens for production features.
- Committed slab: reserved pool sized to cover peak promotional weeks (we’ll size conservative and allow for phased ramp).
- Burst buffer: on-demand burst with pre-agreed overage pricing and an optional cap.

Pricing sensitivity construct:
- Define GPU-indexed trigger: reference a public GPU spot index (we use the Redwood GPU index benchmark).
- If index moves up > +15% vs baseline, tiered discount steps compress (e.g., committed discount falls by X points; overage surcharge applies).
- If index down > -15%, BrightMart receives a rebate/credit applied to next quarter billing.

Questions for procurement to clarify:
1) Do you want a firm lock on discount tiers or a floor/ceiling approach?
2) Any minimum notice for invoking index repricing? (we typically want 30 days)

Next: attached workbook (capacity_waterfall.xlsx) has a sample waterfall and a few scenarios: conservative, mid, aggressive. Karthik — can you add the financial sensitivity table (discount deltas) and a suggested exec-approval ladder? Marissa — can you confirm the legal escalation path if we need a non-standard SLA or discount bypass?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_waterfall.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Hart <olivia@brightmart.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q4 + committed capacity question

Sean / Olivia — reviewed the waterfall workbook this morning. A few recommended guardrails and a suggested discount corridor: 

Recommended guardrails (finance lens):
- Commit tiers: 100k GPU-hours, 250k GPU-hours, 500k GPU-hours (quarterly equivalents).
- Discount corridor (baseline GPU cost = $0.65/hr):
  - If GPU cost <= $0.65/hr: committed discount = 28%
  - If GPU cost in (0.65, 0.75]: discount = 24%
  - If GPU cost in (0.75, 0.85]: discount = 18% and BrightMart gets priority burst credit of 5% on overage
  - If GPU cost > 0.85/hr: discounts reduce by additional 4 points and we require exec approval for any concessions

Contingency and approvals:
- For moves > +20% (risk region), propose an "exec bypass" flow: Sales ops -> VP Sales -> CFO sign-off required for any additional discount beyond floor.
- For moves < -20% we issue a one-time quarterly credit applied to the following invoice.

Quick math example (attached sheet): at 250k tier, a +20% GPU price increase would change unit economics by ~14% margin hit to Redwood if discount holds — we should reserve the right to adjust discounts or minimum commit size.

Operational asks to legal/compliance: define notification cadence (30-day look ahead + monthly settlement) and an audit trail for GPU-index reference.

Olivia — if this corridor looks reasonable we can formalize in a term sheet and route for procurement review.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this is clean and actionable. A few operational/approval notes: 

1) Discount authority matrix: for the 100k and 250k tiers the Director level (me) can approve up to 3% additional concession on a case-by-case basis with written rationale. Anything beyond that routes to the VP Sales + Finance.

2) SLA exception: If BrightMart requests a hard cap on overage charges (no more than X% over committed spend) we need a cross-functional exception and a clear clawback or rebate mechanism for sustained high GPU costs. Legal should draft a clause that references the GPU index, notification timelines, and credit computation.

3) Timeline: I will route the draft term sheet and the waterfall workbook to Finance and Legal tomorrow (9/21) for fast review. If all goes well, we should have a procurement-ready term sheet for BrightMart by 9/24.

Olivia — expect the draft (redwood_commit_draft_20260915.pdf) in the morning; please confirm if procurement wants a monthly or quarterly settlement cadence for index adjustments.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
